title: Salt and Oath
premise: When the border wards of Vhalen collapse on the night the stars vanish, beast-speaker Freya Almeida discovers her forbidden gift is the only thing that can hear what is truly speaking through King Aldric's crown: a memory-eating entity called the Hollow Choir, which has been devouring the kingdom's past to fuel its long winter. Freya must ally with a disgraced ward-keeper and the king's estranged daughter to reach the throne before midwinter seals the Choir's dominion forever. In the end, Freya learns the Choir was once a speaker like herself, betrayed by an earlier crown; she breaks it not with power but by giving it back its stolen name — at the cost of her own memories of the man she loves.
about_author: Dominic Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coastal folklore before turning to fiction. He writes in a drafty house on the northern moors, where he claims the wind dictates half his dialogue.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Selling charms in the market city of Dunmark, Freya senses animals panicking hours before the border wards shatter and every star vanishes at once. She hides her gift as refugees flood in, but a dying gull speaks a warning meant for her by name. Emotional beat: dread beneath ordinary life, the moment hiding stops being possible.

chapters.title: What the Gulls Knew
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the gull's warning to the harbor, Freya finds a drowned ward-stone and meets Torv Askeland, a disgraced ward-keeper drunk on guilt over the wards' failure. He recognizes her gift when she calms a stampeding cart-horse. Emotional beat: reluctant connection between two people keeping secrets.

chapters.title: A Summons Sealed in Salt
chapters.summary: Torv's POV. A royal courier arrives bearing a summons written on salt-preserved vellum — the old magic, outlawed for twelve years. Torv realizes someone at court knows about speakers and is gathering them. He decides to bring Freya, both to protect and to use her. Emotional beat: betrayal dressed as duty.

chapters.title: The Road Through Silent Country
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Traveling north, they pass villages where no birds sing and elders have forgotten their children's names. Freya hears the silence itself chewing. First glimpse that something eats memory, not just sound. Emotional beat: creeping horror, homesickness for things already forgotten.

chapters.title: The Crown That Listens
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In the capital of Haldmere, Aldric struggles against the voice in his crown, which offers him peace in exchange for memories. He has already forgotten his late wife's face. His daughter, Princess Isolde, watches him with suspicion she cannot name. Emotional beat: tragic erosion of a decent man.

chapters.title: Gates of Haldmere
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Arriving at court, Freya is tested by the Lord Protector Serane, who claims to serve the king but wears a hollow smile. Freya conceals her gift during the test but notices the palace dogs refuse to enter the throne room. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Isolde's Ledger
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The princess reveals she has kept a secret ledger of everything her father has forgotten — dates, faces, laws — and the list accelerates. She recruits Freya not as a charm-seller but as a diagnostician of the crown. Emotional beat: grief converted into methodical rebellion.

chapters.title: Audience with a Hollow King
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Brought before Aldric, Freya's gift slips loose: she hears the crown whispering in a chorus of stolen voices. The king, lucid for one moment, begs her silently for help before his eyes glaze. Emotional beat: compassion for the enemy's hostage.

chapters.title: Serane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. The Lord Protector privately offers Freya safety and wealth if she will let the Choir finish — revealing Serane sold the kingdom's memories years ago to escape a plague that took her family. Emotional beat: villainy rooted in wound, temptation made reasonable.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Torv's POV. Torv and Isolde find the sealed royal archive, where pre-outlawry records show the crown was forged from a bound speaker — the first victim of the Choir. The wards were never protection; they were a cage lid. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes history.

chapters.title: What Was Taken from Me
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya discovers a gap in her own past: twelve years ago, the purge that outlawed magic erased her mother — and everyone's memory of her. Only Freya's gift preserved a trace. Her stake becomes personal. Emotional beat: rage and mourning for a person no one else remembers.

chapters.title: Midwinter Begins
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The long winter falls early and hard; snow carries whispers that lull citizens into forgetting mid-task. Riots break out as people lose names mid-sentence. The palace locks down. Emotional beat: society unraveling, urgency crystallized.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Confession
chapters.summary: Serane's POV. Cornered by Isolde with the archive evidence, Serane confesses the mechanism: the Choir feeds through oath-bound loyalty. Every sworn soldier, every loyal subject, is a straw in its mouth. Loyalty itself is the vector. Emotional beat: thematic gut-punch — devotion weaponized.

chapters.title: Breaking Oaths
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. To weaken the Choir, Freya publicly releases soldiers from their oaths using a speaker's rite, knowing it brands her a traitor. Some refuse release, choosing loyalty even now. Torv stands beside her and swears a new kind of oath — freely given, easily broken. Emotional beat: love expressed as chosen, unforced faithfulness.

chapters.title: Flight to the Salt Coast
chapters.summary: Freya, Torv, and Isolde flee Haldmere for the salt coast where the first speaker was bound, pursued by oath-sworn hunters whose eyes have gone white. Isolde is wounded covering their escape. Emotional beat: cost made flesh; the party frays under sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Drowned Shrine
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At low tide they enter the drowned shrine and find the binding circle, still warm after three hundred years. Freya makes contact with the Choir's original self: a girl named Sefa, betrayed by kings who feared her voice. Emotional beat: pity displacing terror.

chapters.title: Sefa's Name
chapters.summary: Interleaved flashbacks (Sefa's POV) with present-tense siege at the shrine. The hunters close in as Freya learns the unbinding requires returning Sefa's true name — which means a speaker must carry it, trading away equal memory. Emotional beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: The Crown Comes South
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. The Choir, threatened, marches the king himself to the shrine, wearing him like armor. Inside, Aldric surfaces one last time and begs Isolde to do whatever is needed. Father and daughter share a final lucid exchange. Emotional beat: heartbreak before the climax.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Climax. Amid battle at the shrine, Freya takes Sefa's name into herself and speaks the unbinding. The Choir unravels; the crown cracks; Aldric collapses free but broken. Freya begins losing her own memories as payment — starting with Torv. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: What Freya Forgot
chapters.summary: Torv's POV. The stars return. Torv watches Freya look at him with polite blankness while she remembers everything else — her mother, her gift, her purpose. He chooses to introduce himself again rather than explain. Emotional beat: quiet devastation, tenderness without self-pity.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Rewritten
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Months later, a regency governs while Aldric relearns how to be a man. Magic is debated openly for the first time in generations. Isolde archives the truth of the Choir so no one can forget it again. Emotional beat: cautious institutional hope.

chapters.title: Salt and Oath
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the Dunmark shore, Freya sells small charms again, but now openly, and keeps a journal of everything so nothing is ever taken unwitnessed. Torv brings her tea each morning, introducing himself anew, and each day she chooses to learn him again. Emotional beat: memory rebuilt by choice — loyalty freely given, the book's thesis embodied.
